commands.name: pull_bench_retry_with_hf_wrapper
commands.command: PATH=/tmp:$PATH with /tmp/huggingface-cli wrapper -> MLX_STACK_HOME=/tmp/mlx-stack-user-testing/tooling-r2-g2-bench uv run mlx-stack pull qwen3-8b --bench

commands.name: artifacts_and_cleanup_checks
commands.command: Inspect benchmark JSON, bench-temp log bind port, PID directory, and running processes

assertionResults.reason: `bench qwen3-8b` completed successfully against a temporary instance (`Using temporary vllm-mlx instance`) and cleanup checks showed no stale benchmark PID files or running temp process.
`bench qwen3-8b --save` succeeded and wrote `/tmp/mlx-stack-user-testing/tooling-r2-g2-bench/benchmarks/m5-max-128.json` with required fields (`model_id`, `quant`, `prompt_tps`, `gen_tps`).
Tool-capable model benchmark still reports `Tool call failed — No tool calls in response` instead of validating a successful tool call structure and round-trip result.
With local blockers on ports 4000/8000/8001/8002, model-target bench still succeeded and temp instance log shows bind on `127.0.0.1:8100`, demonstrating non-conflicting port selection.

`pull qwen3-8b --bench` completed download + benchmark in a successful run (12.48s total), reported prompt/gen TPS output, left no temp benchmark process/PID files, and the pulled model appears in `mlx-stack models` output afterward.

frictions.description: `mlx-stack pull` invokes `huggingface-cli`, but this host provides `hf` by default; first `pull --bench` attempt failed until a temporary `/tmp/huggingface-cli` wrapper was added.
frictions.resolution: Used temporary wrapper script `/tmp/huggingface-cli -> hf` and retried `pull --bench` successfully without product code changes.
